five_minutes: ECB wage tracker signals accelerating pay growth into 2027, threatening to delay Eurozone rate cuts and support euro yields.
Hurricane Isaias advanced toward US Gulf Coast energy hubs, triggering physical production shut-ins and raising immediate crude supply risks.
Indian banking system liquidity eased as RBI VRRR absorption collapsed to ₹1,180 crore while overnight money-market rates softened to 5.44%.
Government 364-day T-bill yields cleared at 6.6485% while RBI rejected all bids for 182-day paper to cap six-month borrowing costs.
RBI delegated FEMA compounding powers to its Regional Offices, streamlining regulatory enforcement for cross-border transactions.

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: ECB wage tracker signals accelerating 2027 pay growth, threatening to delay Eurozone rate cuts
items.what_happened: The ECB's wage tracker indicates slightly higher wage growth across the first three quarters of 2027 compared with full-year 2026 levels.
items.why_it_matters: Resilient forward wage growth threatens sticky services inflation in Europe, pushing out the timeline for ECB policy easing and providing underlying yield support to the euro against the US dollar.

items.headline: Global refinery throughput rebounds by 1.8m b/d post-Q2 slump, capping refined product margin expansion
items.what_happened: Global refinery inputs dropped 4.8 million barrels per day (6%) in Q2 2026 following Middle East conflict before recovering by 1.8 million b/d in Q3 according to Kpler data via EIA.
items.why_it_matters: The partial recovery in refining throughput restores refined fuel supply to global markets, capping crack spreads and dampening gross refining margin upside for Indian state refiners and global oil majors.

items.headline: Banking liquidity surges as RBI VRRR absorption collapses to ₹1,180 crore
items.what_happened: In the 1-day VRRR auction held on November 04, 2026, banks tendered only ₹1,180 crore against a ₹25,000 crore notified amount, all accepted at a 5.49% cutoff rate.
items.why_it_matters: VRRR absorption dropped sharply from ₹23,905 crore yesterday, signalling that commercial banks are holding onto cash balances and short-term surplus liquidity in the interbank system is diminishing.

items.headline: RBI forms Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets to modernise market infrastructure
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank of India constituted the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM) to advise on market structure and technological infrastructure.
items.why_it_matters: Establishes a dedicated formal advisory body to guide upcoming regulatory changes in money, fixed income, and forex market architecture.

items.headline: RBI launches November Household Inflation Expectations Survey across 19 cities
items.what_happened: RBI initiated the November 2026 round of its Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH), capturing subjective price assessment across 19 major urban centers.
items.why_it_matters: Household inflation expectations are a key input for the MPC's real rate assessments and consumer sentiment outlook ahead of the upcoming monetary policy decision.

items.headline: Short-term sovereign yields anchor as 364-day T-bills clear at 6.6485% while 182-day bids are rejected
items.what_happened: RBI auctioned ₹8,000 crore of 91-day T-bills at 5.8970% yield and ₹7,000 crore of 364-day T-bills at 6.6485% yield, while rejecting all bids for the ₹8,000 crore 182-day paper.
items.why_it_matters: The complete rejection of 182-day bids shows the RBI's unwillingness to validate higher yield demands in the six-month segment, maintaining a tight cap on short-term sovereign borrowing benchmarks.

items.headline: Overnight money market rates ease to 5.44%, reflecting softer short-term liquidity conditions
items.what_happened: RBI reported money market operations volume of ₹7.55 lakh crore with a weighted average rate of 5.44% across overnight call, repo, and triparty segments.
items.why_it_matters: Softened further from the 5.60% average recorded yesterday, bringing short-term money market funding costs closer to the central bank's policy repo rate.

items.headline: RBI delegates FEMA compounding powers to Regional Offices, streamlining cross-border compliance resolution
items.what_happened: RBI issued AP (DIR Series) Circular No 28 delegating the compounding of specified FEMA 1999 contraventions directly to its Regional Offices.
items.why_it_matters: Decentralizes enforcement for foreign exchange non-compliance, allowing your corporate clients to resolve technical cross-border filing lapses locally with significantly lower legal friction.
items.action: Review active client FEMA non-compliance files to identify cases eligible for direct compounding at local RBI Regional Offices.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: SEBI introduces cooling-off period for Private listed InvIT Offer for Sale transactions
items.what_happened: SEBI issued a regulatory framework introducing a cooling-off period for sponsors and unitholders executing Offers for Sale (OFS) in privately listed Infrastructure Investment Trusts.
items.why_it_matters: Prevents rapid secondary market churn and sponsor exits in private InvIT structures, directly impacting exit structuring and lock-in covenants for private equity and institutional real estate clients.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: Hurricane Isaias approaches Gulf Coast landfall, triggering shut-ins across crude infrastructure
items.what_happened: Category 2 Hurricane Isaias is expected to make landfall on the US Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, forcing operators to shut in energy production infrastructure.
items.why_it_matters: Firmed further after yesterday's threat warning as physical production shut-ins begin, creating temporary US Gulf supply tightness and putting upward pressure on your Brent crude import cost assumptions.
